newsitem.title: USA: U.S. HEADLINE STOCKS - Issues to Watch - Sept 17.
newsitem.headline: U.S. HEADLINE STOCKS - Issues to Watch - Sept 17.

text.p: -- Intel Corp, the world's largest semiconductor maker, said late Monday it expects third quarter revenues to be better than previously forecast and higher than the second quarter's $4.62 billion.
Intel shares closed at 88-3/8 on Monday and rose 3-3/8 in after-hours trading to 92.

-- Federal Express Corp said lower international air freight yields and higher fuel prices hurt its earnings for the fiscal first quarter. It posted third quarter earnings of $1.08 a share after the market close Monday.

-- Health Systems International Inc is the party involved in merger talks with Foundation Health Corp, the Wall Street Journal reported. Health Systems closed up 3/4 to 26-3/4. Foundation closed off 1-3/4 to 34.
-- IBM Corp plans to offer job buyouts to between 3,000 and 5,000 employees, the New York Times said. IBM closed up 5/8 to 122-3/4.
-- Daniel Industries Inc and Bettis Corp agreed to merge through a swap of 0.58 Daniel share for each Bettis share.
Bettis closed unchanged at 6-7/8, while Daniel fell 1/8 to 13.
-- Pyramid Breweries Inc said it will post disappointing third-quarter earnings of $0.08 to $0.10 a share after weak summer beer sales. Analysts had expected earnings of $0.15 a share, it said.

-- Ball Corp said it will sell its 42 percent stake in Ball-Foster Glass Container Co to its partner in the joint venture, French glassmaker Compagnie de Saint-Gobain, for about $190 million. Ball closed at 24-5/8.
-- Shares of Philip Morris Cos Inc rose after a judge dismissed all pre-1994 claims in a Medicaid lawsuit brought against the tobacco industry by the state of Florida.
